That on 12.11.2020 at about 7.00 p.m. deceased Hanumantha H. slowly and cautiously moving on cycle SCCH 5 at Gorguntepalya junction, Tumkur road,
Bengaluru, meantime a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05AA3114 came in high speed from MES Ring Road and dashed against him, out of the said accident, Hanumantha sustained grievous injuries all over the body, so that, he was shifted to ESIC Hospital,
then shifted to Sapthagiri Hospital, thereafter shifted to Victoria Hospital, then brought to ESIC hospital, wherein he succumbed to the injuries on 01.12.2020, then dead body was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, postmortem is conducted, then taken to their home and conducted funeral ceremony by spending an amount of Rs.50,000/, also they have spent an amount of Rs.1,00,000/ for medical expenses.
3. At the time of accident, deceased Hanumanthappa was aged about 56 years, working as security at Rite Man Protection Force Pvt. Ltd., and SCCH 5 earning Rs.20,000/ p.m. due to this accident

Out of this accident, crime No.99/2020 is registered against the lorry and its driver before Yeshwanthpura traffic police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.

R1 is insurer, R2 is owner of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

During pendency of the petition, petitioner No.1/his wife is died, so that, her son by name Santhosh H. is brought on record as her legal representative as per petitioner No.3.
5.

On service of notice, R1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the SCCH 5 petitioners and admitted the issuance of insurance policy pertains to lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05AA3114 and existence of the said policy at the time of accident, taken contention that, there is no negligency of the lorry driver, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the deceased, he is entitled to take shelter available under Sec.147, 149 of M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act, he is liable to pay compensation subject to compliance of policy conditions by the R2, all the allegations made by the petitioners shall be strictly proved by them, claim made by the petitioners is higher side, hence petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

Hanumanthappa died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.11.2020 at about 7.00 p.m. near Gorguntepalya Junction, Tumkur Road, Bengaluru due to rash and SCCH 5 negligent driving of one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05AA3114 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
8. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.2 has deposed his evidence as PW1 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, R1 has deposed his evidence as RW1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.

9. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  SCCH 5  following:

: In order to prove their case, petitioner No.2 has deposed her evidence as PW1, in her chiefexamination she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 FIR and complaint, Ex.P.2 sketch it is noticed that, crime is registered against the lorry driver for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC, further it is SCCH 5 noticed that, while turning the lorry on left side in middle of the road, this accident is occurred it reveals that, accident is not occurred on left edge of the road, but it is noticed that, deceased had been moving in Goraguntepalya junction on Tumkur road on a cycle, meantime lorry came from ring road and turned on left side, suddenly dashed against the deceased Hanumantha H.
13.
Further P.M.report speaks that death is caused due to respiratory failure as a result of acute respiratory distress syndrome consequent upon multiple injuries sustained post covid19 status.
Further charge sheet marked at Ex.P.10 speaks that, very accident is occurred only due to neglgiency of the lorry driver Srinivas, S/o.Kalegowda.

Further it is noticed that, at the time of accident said Kalegowda had no SCCH 5 driving licence, hence charge sheet is filed against him for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304A of IPC, Sec.3(1) R/w. 181 of IPC, R2/Sathish, S/o.Subbegowda for the offences punishable under Sec.5 R/w. 180 of IPC.
It all goes to show that, very accident is occurred only due to negligency of the lorry driver, but not by the deceased person.

14. During argument counsel for R1 argued that, there is no eyewitness, but when there is charge sheet against the lorry driver under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that,
petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour. Hence I have answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2: As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was aged about 56 years as on the date of accident.

To prove the said fact, they have produced copy SCCH 5 of aadhar card of deceased which is not marked, accordingly he is born on 01.01.1963 and the alleged accident is occurred on 12.11.2020, accordingly age of the deceased is considered about 57 years as on the date of accident,
hence multiplier 9 is applicable with reference to Sarla Verma case.
16. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as security at Rite Man Protection Force Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.

Hanumantha H.
During pendency of the petition, petitioner No.1 is dead.
Petitioner No.2 and 3 have produced copy of aadhar cards marked as Ex.P.11, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to 3 persons, then 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that,
1/3rd of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,76,749/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
23.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.141522023400000374, which is valid for the period from 28.02.2020 to 27.02.2021, the alleged accident was occurred on 12.11.2020, it reveals that, as on the date of accident insurance policy was in force and said fact is admitted by crossexamination by the counsel for R1.
Further driver of the lorry had no driving licence at the SCCH 5 time of the accident.

Under such circumstances, naturally R2/owner is liable to pay the compensation in favour of petitioner, but as per the observations made and findings given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd.
V/s. Swarna Singh and other reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531 and in case of Pappu and another V/s.
Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to issue directions against R1 Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioner by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and recover from the R2/owner through process of law.
Accordingly, I have answered above Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
